title: HostedAPI latency signal-loss synthesis and on-call runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This is a working synthesis of the P0-like latency surge on hosted-api that started 2028-12-04 03:14 UTC and observed intermittent streaming fragmentation and elevated 5xx rates through 2028-12-05. Impact: increased p95/p99 tail latency for text generation endpoints (~3-7x above SLO for 40m windows), ~8% uplift in 500 responses for streaming sessions, and a spike in dropped stream fragments.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture the on-call timeline and investigative commands (notes to self)
- Draft a concise runbook for future signal-loss / telemetry-gap incidents
- Record suspected root-cause, evidence, and follow-ups for engineering teams

High-level hypothesis (short):
A transient collapse in the telemetry aggregation pipeline (edge->ingest) caused the autoscaler and adaptive-batching controller to make poor decisions. That led to a brief period of underprovisioned workers per shard, increased queueing, and streaming fragment reorder/drops at the edge. A mis-sized fallback policy prevented the control-plane from switching to a safe low-batch low-latency profile quickly.

Timeline (UTC, approximate):
- 2028-12-04 03:12: alerting: hosted-api latency-signal (p95) crosses 1200ms threshold
- 03:14: first on-call page. Oncall (Marco) triaged: looked at edge error-summaries and noted increased reconnects
- 03:20: SRE opened INC-4521 and toggled adaptive-batching to conservative mode (manual override) using /api/v1/config/overrides
- 03:26: partial recovery seen in p95 but intermittent 5xx continued for streaming sessions
- 03:40: found ingestion lag in telemetry pipeline: aggregator consumer lag on telemetry-indexer (kafka consumer group) ~6 minutes
- 03:51: control-plane health showed increased latency reading metrics from ingestion; autoscaler scale decisions took >45s to propagate
- 04:10: fallback rate-limiter threshold triggered but the fallback policy had incorrect precedence and did not apply to streaming routes
- 04:37: manual route-level fallback applied (route -> smaller model / lower-batch) — error rate reduced to baseline over 20m window
- 05:10: incident declared resolved-warm; post-incident investigation began.

Detection and signals used:
- Pager alerts from hosted-api-alerting (p95, 5xx ratio, stream-fragment-drop-rate)
- Edge proxy metrics: connection_retries, stream_fragment_drops, stream_reconnect_rate
- Control plane logs: adaptive-batching decisions, autoscaler events, config-override audit trail
- Telemetry ingestion: kafka consumer lag, indexing error rates, ingestion-backpressure metrics

Commands & quick checks oncall ran (notes):
- edge tail: kubectl -n edge logs -l app=edge-proxy --since=15m | jq -r '.level, .msg' | grep -i fragment
- control plane: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/status | jq .adaptiveBatching.lastDecision
- kafka lag: ./kafka-consumer-lag.sh telemetry-indexer | grep -E "consumer-group|lag"
- autoscaler events: kubectl -n serving get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler -o wide

Evidence collected:
- telemetry-indexer consumer lag correlated exactly with window where autoscaler decisions were delayed (03:25-04:05).
- adaptive-batching logs show a frequency of large-batch decisions during the lag window because recent metrics were stale, the controller thought load was low.
- edge proxy logs show increased fragment reassembly failures starting at 03:16 with bursts matching cluster-level queue latency spikes.
- fallback policy config found that streaming routes were excluded from route fallbacks due to an old exception (config ID: fb-exclude-streaming-2027).

Immediate mitigations taken:
- manual conservative override of adaptive-batching at 03:20 (reduced batch sizes across serving nodes)
- applied route-level fallback at 04:37 to send streaming sessions to low-latency variant
- restarted telemetry-indexer consumer group (graceful restart) at 03:48 — this collapsed lag and allowed control-plane to observe fresh metrics

Why the rollbacks were slow:
- the autoscaler requires two consecutive windows of aggregated metrics to make downward/upward decisions; with ingestion lag it used stale low-util reports leading to overpacking of requests into fewer workers
- fallback precedence bug: exception list for routing fallbacks had priority over global fallback, which meant automated fallback did not triage streaming traffic until manual intervention

Draft runbook (for signal-loss / telemetry-gap -> latency cascade):
1) Pager triggers on p95 above 1000ms or stream-fragment-drop-rate > 0.5%
2) Oncall: check telemetry ingestion lag immediately: ./kafka-consumer-lag.sh telemetry-indexer
   - if lag > 2m -> run restart sequence for telemetry-indexer: k rollout restart deployment/telemetry-indexer -n ingest
3) Put adaptive-batching into conservative mode: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/config/overrides -d '{"mode":"conservative","expires":"+30m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN'
4) Apply temporary route-level fallback for streaming routes: controlplane CLI: rctl apply-fallback --route streaming-* --profile low-latency --reason "telemetry-lag"
5) Observe edge proxy metrics for fragment drops for 15m window; if no improvement, escalate to serving-runtime oncall
6) After telemetry lag resolves, remove overrides and monitor for oscillation for at least 1 hour.

Notes on runbook design choices:
- conservative adaptive-batching is cheaper to apply quickly and reduces tail risk (lower batch sizes lead to lower p99 latency even if throughput drops slightly)
- route-level fallbacks are used as a last-resort for streaming because streaming sessions are more sensitive to fragment loss than short generation calls

Instrumentation gaps uncovered (follow-up items):
- control-plane should have a direct circuit breaker visible metric when telemetry ingestion lag > threshold (currently only internal logs)
- fallback precedence rules are opaque in the current config UI; make an audit table for fallback exceptions and add unit tests to ensure streaming routes are not accidentally excluded
- we lacked a synthetic streaming-canary that exercises long-lived multiplexed sessions at the edge — add a canary job to run 24/7 and alert on fragment reassembly failures

Follow-ups / Actions (owners assigned):
- eng-sre: add telemetry-lag gauge to global control-plane dashboard (owner: Marco, due 2028-12-12)
- serving-runtime: tighten autoscaler metric windows to be resilient to 2–3m ingestion lag (owner: Jinsoo, due 2029-01-05)
- platform: add unit test for fallback precedence logic and rollout fix (owner: Lena, due 2028-12-19)
- dx/devex: create a short runbook playbook card in Console "If telemetry lag, set adaptive-batching conservative" (owner: Aisha, due 2028-12-10)

On-call lessons learned (voice-of-oncall):
- we need a single-pane-of-glass quick-check that shows (1) telemetry lag, (2) adaptive-batching current mode, (3) fallback exceptions for streaming routes — current investigation required switching between 4 dashboards
- manual overrides were effective, but the audit trail was sparse — add a required reason field on override API (helps later RCA)

Appendix: useful links and quick commands (keep in runbook card):
- kafka consumer lag script: ops/bin/kafka-consumer-lag.sh telemetry-indexer
- control plane override endpoint: https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/config/overrides
- route fallback CLI: rctl apply-fallback --route <pattern> --profile <profile>
- escalate: pageduty -> eng-sre -> serving-runtime -> platform

Raw oncall notes (copied from Slack/incident channel):
- 03:15 Marco: seeing fragment drops on /v1/stream generate, p95 shot to 1.3s
- 03:22 Aisha: pushed conservative batch override, will monitor
- 03:48 Jinsoo: restarted telemetry-indexer, consumer lag down to ~15s
- 04:02 Lena: found fallback exclusion rule, patch in progress to make precedence explicit

Open questions for post-incident deep dive:
- why did the telemetry-indexer consumer lag spike? (network blips vs GC pause vs broker-side rebalance)
- should autoscaler be tolerant to short-lived ingestion lag windows (configurable grace period)?

This is a working draft — please add notes inline. Once consensus reached we'll convert to formal postmortem with timeline artifacts and metrics screenshots and update the incident severity to P0 if needed.
